fields.statement: Built 3c614aeb to a scratch binary and, in a scratch git repo with RHIZA_* unset, added intents m1 (milestone=1), umb and umb2 (umbrella=yes), and proposed change sets U (serves umb), V (serves m1 and umb), U2 (serves umb2), W (serves m1) and X (serves nothing). rhiza roadmap --json gave groups milestone m1 [W], backlog [X], umbrella umb [U, V], umbrella umb2 [U2] in that order. V appears only under umb, not under m1. The human rhiza roadmap printed '## m1', '## Backlog', '## umb', '## umb2', and rhiza api call roadmap '{}' gave the same bytes as roadmap --json. go test -run TestScripts/(roadmap-umbrella|describe-golden) passes.

In the same scratch repo I accepted U, W and U2. rhiza ready --json marked U and U2 not ready with reason 'umbrella: work is carved out of it', marked V with that reason plus 'not accepted: proposed', and W was ready with next = W. The human rhiza ready printed 'next: ... W milestone' and listed the umbrella reason under each umbrella change set. go test ./internal/api passes, including TestUmbrellaNotReady.

Ran the scratch binary's rhiza tui app roadmap in a real Rex terminal pane over the same repo and drove it with send-key. Collapsed, it showed '+ umb (2 change sets)' and '+ umb2 (1 change set)' with no member rows. j reached the umb row, and enter turned it into '- umb' with U and V listed below, with their not-ready reasons. j moved onto U, and enter opened U's detail. esc went back, and r kept the cursor on U with the group still expanded. k then enter collapsed it again, and r kept the cursor on the umb row. a, p, s and o on a header row do nothing. tui app roadmap --once printed the same bytes as rhiza roadmap --json, and cmd/rhiza/tui.go is unchanged. go test ./internal/tui/roadmapapp passes.
